claims.text: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has excellent mechanical performance at 1600 °C.
Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has very poor room-temperature ductility.
Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has irradiation resistance predicted by first-principles calculations.
Substitution with approximately 5 at.% V will preserve a single-phase BCC structure.
Approximately 5 at.% V substitution will cause V to segregate preferentially to grain boundaries.
V grain-boundary segregation will create localized softening zones within the BCC matrix.
V has a smaller atomic size than Nb, Mo, Ta, and W.
V has a lower elastic modulus than Nb, Mo, Ta, and W.
The smaller atomic size and lower elastic modulus of V drive its preferential segregation to NbMoTaW grain boundaries.
V segregation lowers local barriers for dislocation nucleation and motion at room temperature.
Localized grain-boundary softening will significantly increase room-temperature elongation to failure and fracture toughness relative to undoped NbMoTaW.
The V-doped alloy will maintain mechanical strength at 1600 °C comparable to undoped NbMoTaW.
The V-doped alloy will retain irradiation-defect recombination characteristics comparable to those of undoped NbMoTaW.
The V-doped alloy will exhibit irradiation resistance comparable to undoped NbMoTaW as assessed through defect evolution.
Keeping the V content near 5 at.% will avoid secondary phases and deleterious segregation.
Excessive V content may destabilize the phase constitution or compromise high-temperature properties.
V contents substantially below approximately 5 at.% may be insufficient to alter grain-boundary behavior measurably.

contradictions.description: The conditions require homogeneous V distribution, whereas the proposed mediator and mechanism require preferential V enrichment at grain boundaries. These can coexist only if 'homogeneous' refers to macroscale composition rather than atomic-scale distribution, but that distinction is not stated.
